topic: A Manitoba CCPC earns $100,000 before paying its owner (2026): all salary vs all non-eligible dividends; what the cash difference buys (CPP, RRSP room); mixing; EI exclusion for >40% shareholders

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): single Manitoba owner, no other income, CCPC eligible for the small business deduction; salary set so salary + employer CPP = $100,000; EI premiums not included (owner controls more than 40% of voting shares); RRSP room = 18% of 2026 earned income, usable from 2027, subject to the annual dollar limit. Computed by c2/calc.py.

sources.dividends: as c1/data.json: ITA 82(1)(b)(i) gross-up 15%, s.121 federal DTC 9/13; Manitoba Income Tax Act s.4.7(1)(b)(i.2) 0.7835%
sources.salary: salary is employment income taxed at 2026 federal/Manitoba rates (CRA T4127 2026); Canada employment amount $1,501; employee CPP 5.95% + CPP2 4% with enhanced portion deductible (line 22215), employer pays a matching amount
sources.cpp: CPP Act ss.12–13: contributions on salary/wages (both employee and employer shares) build CPP pensionable earnings; dividends are not contributory
sources.rrsp: ITA 146(1) 'RRSP deduction limit': lesser of the RRSP dollar limit and 18% of the previous year's earned income (employment income counts, dividends do not); laws.justice.gc.ca current to 2026-09-30
sources.ei: Employment Insurance Act s.5(2)(b): insurable employment does not include employment by a corporation of a person who controls more than 40% of its voting shares
sources.corp: CCPC small business rate 9% federal + 0% Manitoba (c3 R1); salary is deductible to the corporation, so no corporate tax remains when all profit is paid as salary + employer CPP
